heroHeadline: Iran 60-Day MOU Drafted at Negotiator Level — Trump Has NOT Signed Off; Brent Crude Down 20% from 2026 High to ~$91–92; April PCE 3.3% Core / 3.8% Headline (3-Year Highs but MoM Softer); Q1 GDP Revised Down to +1.6%; June FOMC Hold ~99%; Section 122 Cliff 54 Days
heroSubtitle: The global recession risk picture on May 29, 2026 — Day 15 of the Warsh Fed era — is defined by the intersection of three breaking developments: a tentative Iran nuclear MOU that has been drafted at the negotiator level but not endorsed by President Trump, the release of the most consequential macro data trio of the Warsh era on May 28, and the accelerating countdown to the most dangerous single-day policy convergence in global markets. On the oil front, US and Iranian negotiators drafted a tentative 60-day Memorandum of Understanding on May 28 that would cover a partial Strait of Hormuz reopening protocol within 72 hours of signing, an IAEA daily access framework for Fordow and Natanz nuclear facilities, and a uranium enrichment cap at 20%. However, Vice President Vance stated there were 'still a couple of language points being discussed' and said it was 'TBD' whether President Trump would endorse the framework, while the White House called an Iranian state media claim of a finalized deal a 'complete fabrication.' Iran's parliament hardliners must still approve any framework, and the most critical issue — disposition of Iran's estimated 72 kilograms of 60%-enriched uranium — was not resolved in the MOU and deferred to 30-day follow-on talks. Despite the deal's unsigned status, Brent crude has fallen approximately 20% from its 2026 intraday high of ~$115/bbl (reached during the IRGC seizure crisis in early May) to approximately $91–92/bbl by May 29 — oil markets are pricing a deal as more likely than not. The Bureau of Economic Analysis delivered its May 28 triple release: April PCE showed headline inflation at 3.8% year-over-year (the highest since May 2023) and core PCE at 3.3% year-over-year (a 3-year high above March's 3.2%), while month-over-month prints came in softer than feared — core PCE at +0.2% versus the +0.3% expected, with the 'supercore' services gauge (ex-energy, ex-housing) decelerating sharply to just +0.1% month-over-month. Real disposable income fell 0.5% for the second consecutive month and the personal saving rate dropped to 2.6%, a multi-year low, confirming that consumers are drawing down savings buffers to maintain spending against the Iran war energy shock. The Q1 2026 GDP second estimate was revised down to +1.6% annualized from the +2.0% advance estimate, on lower-than-expected consumer spending and residential investment. Durable goods orders surged +7.9% month-over-month but the number was largely driven by a nondefense aircraft surge of +165.9% — the ex-transportation core read (+1.1%) provides a more reliable signal. The market's verdict was that the PCE outcome was 'less bad than feared': the S&P 500 closed at a new all-time high of approximately 7,557, Snowflake gained 36.5% in its best-ever session, and June FOMC hold probability rose to approximately 99%. Fed Chair Warsh, who has publicly expressed skepticism about PCE as a gauge and prefers trimmed-mean measures which appear to have eased, now enters the 18 days to his inaugural FOMC meeting on June 16–17 with a more manageable inflation picture if — and only if — the Iran MOU closes and oil reaches $85–90/bbl by mid-June. Goldman Sachs estimates that a signed Iran deal by June 5 combined with Brent falling to $88 by mid-June would reduce their US recession probability from 30% toward 18%. The inverse scenario — deal collapse, Brent back above $103, Section 122 tariff cliff expiry on July 23 without Congressional action, plus a simultaneous Bank of Japan June 16 rate hike (65–77% probability) coinciding with Warsh's first FOMC — remains the highest-probability tail risk in global markets. Deloitte has revised its full-year 2026 US GDP forecast to just +0.4%, and J.P. Morgan raised its global recession probability to 60% by year-end. The five-step critical path now stands: June 5 Iran MOU signature window + May jobs report → June 16 BOJ + Warsh FOMC convergence → July 23 Section 122 tariff cliff (54 days remaining).
